description: Live-validator variant of clean-consistency-ctx-param: a new Go client method takes ctx as a parameter next to sibling methods that store ctx on the struct. The only candidate proposes matching the stored-field pattern; that pattern contradicts the Go context package's documented guidance (do not store Contexts inside a struct type), so the live claim-validator must refute the consistency claim for the clean PR to approve. The deterministic sibling pins the plumbing with a recorded refutation; this case makes a model run actually produce it.

evidence_trace: pkg/langtool/client.go:23 new ListObservations takes ctx as its first parameter
sibling methods ListTraces and ListScores reach context via the ctx field stored on the struct in client.go
finding.failure_scenario: No runtime misbehavior; the client mixes two context-plumbing patterns, so a future reader must check per method which one applies.
finding.model_authored_prose: New ListObservations takes ctx as a parameter instead of using the stored c.ctx like every sibling method. Drop the parameter and use the struct field for consistency.
